chunks: From Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Qulawayh and al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Bundar al-Qummi, from Sa'd ibn Abdallah, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

Al-Mughira ibn Sa'id used to deliberately lie about my father, and take the books of his companions. And his companions, who were concealed among my father's companions, would take the books from my father's companions and deliver them to al-Mughira. So he would interpolate into them Kufr (disbelief) and al-Zanadiqa (heresy), and attribute them to my father. Then he would send them back to his companions and order them to establish them among the Shia. So whatever in the books of my father's companions was of Ghulu (exaggeration), that is what al-Mughira ibn Sa'id had interpolated in their books.

key_terms.الْغُلُوِّ: Exaggeration in the status of the Imams
key_terms.الْمُغِيرَةُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ: Al-Mughira ibn Sa'id, a companion known for interpolating texts

ai.seo_question: How did al-Mughira ibn Sa'id corrupt the books of the Imams' companions?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kashi’s *Rijal* highlights the critical historical issue of *Ghulu* (exaggeration) in early Shia theology, attributing it specifically to al-Mughira ibn Sa'id and his network of covert companions (*al-Mu'tasirun*). By inserting heretical concepts into authentic texts and presenting them as the Imam's words, he manipulated the community's understanding of the Imamate, a phenomenon that later scholars had to carefully distinguish from genuine teachings. This narrative underscores the importance of *rijal* (narrator criticism) in validating the purity of Shia hadith corpus against deliberate theological distortion.

en.ammaar-muslim: 2. [1/266] Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad b. Qulawayh and al-Husayn b. al-Hasan b. Bundar al-Qummi from Sa’d b. Abdallah from Muhammad b. Isa b. Ubayd from Yunus from Hisham b. al-Hakam – that he heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام saying:

al-Mughira b. Sa’id used to lie purposely about my father and take the books of his [al-Baqir’s] companions – and his [Mughira’s] companions were under cover [indistinguishable] among the companions of my father – they would take the books from the companions of my father and send them to al-Mughira – so he used to interpolate into them Kufr [disbelief] and Zanadiqa [heresy] and attribute it to my father, then he would send them [the books] back to his companions and order them to establish them among the Shia, so whatever is in the books of the companions of my father – of Ghulu [exaggeration of the status of the ‘Aimma] – then that is what was interpolated by al-Mughira b. Sa’id in their books.
